notes: soundLAB 1.4.0: hands-free practice. A pedal, a button on your synth (a MODX foot switch or Assign switch) or a Bluetooth page-turner pedal now presses Next, Back and Stop, so you never reach for the screen: start a lesson, show the answer, go to the next question or level, retry, end the run, step a Live set. Set it up in Settings › Hands-free control (press Learn, then the button); a LUMI without a pedal can double-tap its lowest key. The bound button only moves practice on — it never plays, sustains or answers. 1.3.1: the Synth tab never ignores a tap any more. When the Deck or a Live slot cannot reach your synth, a bar says why and fixes it in one tap: Connect MIDI, or pick the synth when the output is the LUMI (on Android, where the app has one MIDI output, the key lights switch off instead of playing notes on the synth). A refused tap now says so on the page, a Live slot no longer shows as loaded when nothing was sent, and the port name is no longer doubled under the sound name. soundLAB 1.3.0: the Synth tab. Your synth gets its own tab with three pills: Deck (a play face with faders instead of knobs, a knob-row picker like the MODX, Assign knobs named after what they control, Scenes, chips and an Explain mode that teaches what each control does), Live (Live sets in pages of 16, foot switch and octave-button stepping, Go live with Lock and Panic, whole-setup profiles you can export and import) and Hub (the MIDI Hub, now with key splits and port-aware rules). Presets save a full snapshot: sound, fader values, colour, the app key and scale, a split. One Open on the Play tab opens a MIDI file, a MusicXML score or a text tab and sends it to the synth, the Woodshed or tab view. The Practice tab is now Train, the clef is a header icon like its neighbours, and long page notes moved into tours and tips.
